# TD-347: split the dashboard bundle before the next UI brief

## The number

```
vite.config.ts  chunkSizeWarningLimit: 560   (Vite kB = 1000 B -> 560_000 B)
app chunk after BR-085                        559_516 B
slack                                             484 B
```

`cli/dashboard/src` builds to ONE chunk. Every layer, page and library lands in
it, so any UI addition is charged against those 484 bytes.

## Why now, and not as a rung on the next brief's cut-ladder

BR-085 spent **132 B** of the 616 B FR-247 left — and it spent them on genuinely
minor client plumbing: a field on a search-row type, a banner's scope source, a
search-params render. That is the signal. **At 484 B, "small UI change" is no
longer automatically affordable**, and the remaining budget is smaller than the
last trivial change.

Two GL-006 briefs are waiting behind this and **cannot both land**:

- **FR-248** — cross-layer search, one box over every layer, RRF-fused.
- **FR-249** — create a goal from the dashboard (the write door's first two-tool
  mutation).

Whichever runs first would otherwise have to own the split as its first step,
which means its review has to adjudicate a bundling change and a feature at the
same time. That is the wrong shape: a split is infrastructure both depend on,
it is independently testable, and its correctness argument (does every route
still reach its data? does the gate still measure the right artifact?) has
nothing to do with either feature.

## Scope

1. **Split by ROUTE, not by size.** The router already knows the layers; lazy
   the layer pages so the initial chunk carries the shell and the router, and
   each layer arrives on navigation. Do not chase the number by extracting
   arbitrary modules — a split that reduces the headline while making a cold
   navigation slower is a regression wearing a smaller number.
2. **Decide what stays eager, and argue it.** The shell, the router, the project
   scope hook and anything on the first paint path. A layer that is nearly
   always the landing view may belong eager too — say which and why rather than
   lazying everything reflexively.
3. **The vendored graph library is the elephant — check it first.** FR-244's
   graph library is bundled, never fetched (that is an AC and must stay true).
   If it dominates the chunk, splitting the graph route is most of the win and
   the rest is noise. Measure the composition before choosing what to move.
4. **Keep the ceiling meaningful after the split.** `chunkSizeWarningLimit`
   currently guards ONE chunk. Once there are several, a per-chunk limit that
   each new small chunk trivially passes measures nothing. Decide what the gate
   asserts post-split — initial-chunk size, total, or both — and make sure it
   still fails for the thing it exists to catch.
5. **Do not weaken any existing gate to make room.** The pack ledger, the
   packed-size hard ceiling (TD-329) and the browser gates stay as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The initial chunk is materially below the limit, with the number measured
      and recorded in the pack ledger.
- [ ] Every route still loads and renders its data — proven by the browser gate,
      not by the build succeeding.
- [ ] The graph library is still bundled and never fetched (FR-244's AC holds).
- [ ] The chunk gate still fails for an oversized initial chunk after the split —
      DEMONSTRATED by planting bulk and showing it red. A gate that passes
      because the thing it measured moved elsewhere is the defect class this
      repo keeps filing.
- [ ] A cold navigation to a lazied route is measured, so the split's cost is on
      the record beside its benefit.
- [ ] The ledger records the new composition, so the next planner sees which
      chunk their change is charged against.

## Out of scope
- FR-248 and FR-249 themselves.
- The packed-tarball ceiling (TD-329) — a different budget, and unaffected by
  how the browser bundle is chunked.
- Retrieval, weights, or any behaviour change. This is purely how the same code
  is delivered.

## Notes

Filed 2026-08-05 on operator decision, after BR-085's byte reading showed the
slack falling from 616 B to 484 B on a small change. The operator was given the
choice between folding the split into whichever UI brief ran first and hunting
it separately, and chose separately.

**Measurement caveat inherited from this session:** on this machine
`npm run build` in `cli/` is a live deploy — the operator's MCP runs the brain
server from `cli/dist` — so the PACKED figure cannot be re-measured mid-review.
`bash cli/scripts/build-dashboard.sh` is safe and is what makes the CHUNK figure
re-measurable; it writes only the gitignored `cli/dist/dashboard`. Use it.

Related: FR-247 (left 616 B), BR-085 (spent 132 of them and took the reading),
TD-329 (the packed ceiling, a different budget), FR-244 (the vendored graph
library that must stay bundled), FR-248 / FR-249 (both blocked on this).
